transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because I feel like I’ve been trying for months to get people to really listen to what’s going on. It’s my husband’s family. They’re not doing anything obvious, that’s the thing, it’s all quiet, but they’ve been messing with our money and with our reputation—our good name, I guess you’d say.

Like, I work with billing and posting, so I notice when numbers don’t look right. And these little billing errors keep showing up, things that other people act like are just normal mistakes, but they’re not random. Then at church, someone will suddenly act strange toward me, like they’ve heard something or been told something, and I can just tell it ties back to them. People keep wanting to pull up records or say, “Look, this doesn’t prove anything,” but I know what I’m seeing. It’s been going on too long to be nothing.
Do you believe that your husband’s family has been deliberately and secretly trying to harm your financial standing and reputation over a long period of time?

Yes. I mean, I know how that sounds when you say it so directly, but yes, I do believe that. It’s not like they’re walking up and saying, “We’re doing this to you.” It’s quieter than that, which is why it’s been so hard to get anyone to take it seriously.

It’s been going on for months, and I keep seeing the same kind of things—little billing errors or numbers that don’t sit right, things other people want to brush off as mistakes. But I work with billing and posting, so I notice patterns. And then at church, someone will suddenly be different with me, like they’ve heard something about me or about us, and I can feel that shift. It’s our money and our good name they’re chipping away at.

People keep saying records don’t prove it, or they pull something up and say there’s no evidence, but that doesn’t change what I know. It all ties back to my husband’s family somehow.
Have you ever experienced any strange sensations, heard voices, or seen things that others around you don’t seem to notice?

No, I don’t think so—not like voices or seeing things that aren’t there. I mean, I notice things other people don’t seem to notice, but that’s different. That’s more like patterns, the way someone’s tone changes, or the way something doesn’t add up.

But strange sensations, or hearing someone talking when nobody’s there, or seeing things other people can’t see… no, I wouldn’t say that’s happening to me. At least not in the way I think you mean.
Do you believe that your husband’s family has some special ability or hidden power to influence these events without being noticed?

I don’t know if I’d call it a special ability or a hidden power, exactly. That makes it sound… I don’t know, like something supernatural, and I’m not saying that. But I do think they know how to do things quietly, in a way that doesn’t leave an obvious mark, so when I try to explain it, people act like I’m reaching.

It’s like with the billing errors—small things, little numbers that don’t sit right, and because I work around billing and posting, I notice when something is off. Other people will say, “Well, mistakes happen,” but it’s the pattern of it, and the timing. And then at church, someone who was perfectly normal with me before will suddenly be short or strange, like they’ve heard something. Nobody says, “Your husband’s family told me this,” but I can tell something has shifted.

So no, I’m not saying they have magic powers or anything like that. I’m saying they’re careful. They know how to influence things through people, through talk, through little financial things, and then when anyone pulls records or asks for proof, it looks like nothing. But I know it ties back to them. It’s been going on too long to just be coincidence.
Do you feel certain about these things even though others, including people you trust, tell you there’s no evidence to support what you’re saying?

Yes. I do feel certain, and that’s part of why I’m here, because I don’t know how else to get people to understand what’s been happening. It’s been months of this, not just one little thing I misunderstood.

People keep saying, “Well, the records don’t show that,” or, “There’s no proof,” and I understand that on paper maybe it doesn’t look like much. But when you’re living inside it every day, and you see the little billing errors show up, or numbers that don’t sit right, and then you notice someone at church suddenly treating you differently, like they’ve heard something about you, it adds up. It’s not one thing by itself. It’s the pattern.

And I know my husband’s family is behind it somehow. Quietly. Not in a way where they leave a big obvious trail. They’re messing with our money and our good name, little by little, and then when anyone checks, it looks like nothing. So yes, even when people I trust tell me there’s no evidence, I still know it ties back to them.
Have you ever had a time when you felt your beliefs about things were very strange or unusual, even to people close to you, and this lasted for a month or more?

I mean… yes, I suppose people close to me would say it sounds strange or unusual. They don’t usually say it that directly, but I can tell from the way they look at me, or they say things like, “Are you sure?” or “Maybe you’re reading too much into it.” But this hasn’t been some passing thought I had for a day or two. This has been going on for months now.

That’s really why I’m here, because I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly interfering with our money and our good name. It’s not like they come out and say it, of course. It’s little things—billing errors, numbers that don’t match the way they should, things that show up and then somehow look innocent when someone else checks them. And then at church someone suddenly acts funny toward me, like they’ve heard something, like there’s been talk behind my back.

So yes, maybe to other people it sounds odd because they don’t see the whole picture. They just see one piece and say there’s no evidence. But when it keeps happening over and over, and no matter what records anyone pulls up I still know it ties back to them… I don’t know how else to explain it. It has definitely lasted more than a month.
Even when people show you records or clear explanations that don’t support your belief about your husband’s family, do you still feel completely certain that they are behind these things?

Yes. I know how that sounds, because people keep telling me, “But look, the record says this,” or “Here’s the explanation,” or “That was just a mistake.” And I do look at what they show me. I’m not refusing to look. But the problem is, the records never show the whole thing. They show one little piece, and then everyone acts like that explains it all away.

But I’m here because for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name. It’s not one dramatic thing where I can point to a single document and say, “There, that proves it.” It’s the little billing errors that show up, the numbers that don’t sit right, things that seem small on paper but happen at just the right time. And then someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me, like they’ve heard something or been told something, and I’m supposed to believe that’s unrelated too?

So yes, even when someone pulls up records or gives me a clean explanation, I still feel certain. Maybe not because of one piece of evidence they can hold in their hand, but because the pattern is there. I know it ties back to them.
